text:
Maya: quick heads-up — our Next.js sample app deployed to Vercel Edge is throwing at runtime: `TypeError: require is not defined` when importing the JS SDK. stack trace points to dist/cjs/index.js

Chris: ugh, classic CJS-in-edge. Did the publish accidentally ship CJS as the default export? can you paste package.json exports?

Maya: here's the relevant bits from the package we installed (from node_modules):
```json
{
  \"main\": \"dist/cjs/index.js\",
  \"module\": \"dist/esm/index.js\",
  \"types\": \"dist/types/index.d.ts\",
  \"exports\": {
    \"./package.json\": \"./package.json\"
  }
}
```

Samir: yeah that explains it — no conditional `exports` mapping for `import` vs `require`. Edge runtimes use ESM, so the bundler/runtime picks `main`? Next/Vercel will sometimes resolve to `main` when exports is sparse.

Alina: also `types` pointing to a separate dist/types dir can confuse TS consumers if types are emitted only for ESM build. We should consolidate.

Maya: reproduction steps I ran locally: `npx vercel@edge dev` -> import `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-sdk'` -> runtime fails with require is not defined. Works fine in node dev.

Chris: options: 1) add conditional exports: \"\"exports\"": { \".\": { \"import\": \"./dist/esm/index.js\", \"require\": \"./dist/cjs/index.js\" } } 2) ship only ESM (and set \"main\" to ESM) and provide a CJS interop entry for Node consumers 3) publish two packages (bad imo)

Samir: I'd push for canonical conditional exports + ensure types point at the ESM d.ts entry. Something like:
```json
\"exports\": {
  \".\": {
    \"types\": \"./dist/esm/index.d.ts\",
    \"import\": \"./dist/esm/index.js\",
    \"require\": \"./dist/cjs/index.js\",
    \"default\": \"./dist/esm/index.js\"
  },
  \"./package.json\": \"./package.json\"
}
```

Alina: also make sure the build writes `dist/esm/index.d.ts` and that bundlers (esbuild/webpack) pick up the import field first. We should run smoke tests against Cloudflare/Vercel edge images.

Maya: Is there risk of Node <14 or older tooling breaking with `exports`? We still support some customers on older Node.

Chris: `exports` is node 12+ but old bundlers might ignore it. For fallback we can keep `main` pointing to CJS for old resolution semantics, and rely on `exports` for modern resolvers. That's the usual dual-pkg pattern.

Samir: note on types: TS resolver doesn't respect `exports.types` until TS 4.7+? So preferred pattern is to have a top-level `types` field that points to a single entry file: \"types\": \"dist/esm/index.d.ts\" and also emit `package.json` exports `types` conditionally as above for tooling that uses exports.

Maya: ok — quick patch idea: update package.json as Samir suggested, rebuild, publish a canary, and verify the Vercel edge sample app. I can try a canary release today if we agree on the exact mapping.

Alina: one more gotcha — sourcemaps path differences between esm and cjs builds caused Node stack traces to show incorrect lines. If we're rebuilding both outputs, run a small script to normalize `sourceMappingURL` paths.

Chris: +1 on canary. Also add a tiny CI job that runs the `examples/next-edge` sample in a headless Vercel dev environment or at least with `@vercel/build-utils` + esbuild to catch runtime `require` errors.

packager-bot: build started for @redwood/sdk@canary-0.1.57 — esm and cjs artifacts will be uploaded to canary registry.

Maya: thanks. I'll try canary, verify both node (CJS) consumers and Next edge sample. Will report back here with logs. If all green, we should make this our default publish layout and add a checklist in release docs.

Samir: and add a short note in SDK README about edge compatibility and suggested bundler config (esbuild target, `resolve.conditions = ['import', 'default']`).

Chris: awesome. If we still see weird interop after the exports fix, we can consider shipping single ESM-only with a separate compatibility shim package, but try to avoid extra packages for now.

Maya: filed a tiny follow-up PR for package.json + build script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/342 — will attach canary once packager-bot finishes.
